// KF3_Cleanup.txt - last-pass fixes applied to the finished ENGLISH by KF3TextFit ([Cleanup] FixList).
//
// WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
// _Substitutions runs before everything else and matches anywhere in a string, so a short Friend name eats
// part of a longer word: ナナ=Nana (substitution 3546) also matches inside バナナ, the translator is handed
// バ{{X}} and answers "Ba Nana". _Postprocessors cannot repair that, because a line that is already in
// _AutoGeneratedTranslations never goes near a postprocessor again - and that cache is most of what a player
// reads. The fixes below are applied at the cache instead, so they reach cached lines, fresh translations and
// the output of r:/sr: rules alike.
//
// This file sits one level ABOVE Text\ on purpose: XUnity scans Text\ and all its subfolders, and would read
// anything in there as translations. Do not move it into Text\.
//
// FORMAT
//   broken=fixed              a literal replacement, case-sensitive, anywhere in the line
//   r:pattern=replacement     a .NET regular expression ($1 for the first group)
//   // comment                ignored, as are blank lines
//   \n                        a line break, on either side, as in XUnity's own files
// Rules run top to bottom and each sees what the one above produced. Keep the list short - it runs on every
// line the translator stores or serves. Spacing faults (a. m., B. C., "Boss' s") are built into the DLL
// already, under [Cleanup] FixSpacing - they do not belong here.
//
// A change here needs a game restart to take effect.

// --- words a substitution broke apart ---
// Copied from the same entries in _Postprocessors.txt, which only reach text on its way back from the
// translator. Here they reach the cache too. The copies in _Postprocessors do no harm; leave or remove them.
// From 2026-11-07 the DLL also stops this happening in the first place - a katakana key of up to 3 characters
// can no longer match inside a longer katakana word ([Substitutions] GuardKatakanaNamesUpTo) - so these only
// matter for lines that were translated before that.
Ba nana=banana
Ba Nana=banana
ba Nana=banana
A Lulu=Alulu
a Lulu=Alulu
a lulu=Alulu

// Add more as you meet them. To find candidates, look for a capitalised Friend name sitting as its own word
// inside what should be one word; the fragment before it is usually one or two syllables of kana.
